directions.description: Train NextItNet with categorical next-item cross-entropy instead of single-negative BPR. The original [NextItNet implementation](https://github.com/fajieyuan/WSDM2019-nextitnet) provides the family-specific reference. Hypothesis: competition against the item vocabulary supplies stronger ranking supervision.
directions.implementation:
Apply each direction separately to the supplied corrected baseline. Shared requirements: DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; training seed 42; unchanged preprocessing seed 0 and supplied splits; exactly 200 batches/epoch and at most 200 epochs, honoring the host's SASREC_EPOCHS=200 default. Retain all four dataset routes, one independently trained NextItNet checkpoint/category, single-GPU execution and trial-local artifacts. Select using pinned macro validation HR@10; do not use test data. Preserve sample_batch's shifted causal targets. Add log2feats(self, sequence) as an alias for encode_sequence, and predict_score(self, features, items) using the same tied item-embedding dot product as forward and score_candidates. Keep the final-nonpadding-position readout. Preserve the predictor writer's import of this trained model class and checkpoint metadata; no averaging or score fusion.

Initial experiment: retain baseline architecture, LR=0.001, batch=128, dropout=0.2. Replace bpr_sequence_loss with:

def categorical_loss(model, seq, pos, neg):
    import torch.nn.functional as F
    valid = pos.ne(0)
    features = model.log2feats(seq)[valid]
    targets = pos[valid] - 1
    # Uniformly subsample supervised positions to bound vocabulary-logit memory.
    if targets.numel() > 512:
        keep = torch.randperm(targets.numel(), device=seq.device)[:512]
        features, targets = features[keep], targets[keep]
    logits = features @ model.item_emb.weight[1:].T
    return F.cross_entropy(logits.float(), targets)

Exclude padding class 0. All nonpadding next-item targets remain eligible for supervision. Inference remains the existing dot product, so the checkpoint architecture and predictor constructor remain unchanged.

directions.description: Increase negatives and replace BPR with calibrated gBCE, transferring only the training objective to NextItNet. The [gSASRec paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.07192) and [official PyTorch implementation](https://github.com/asash/gSASRec-pytorch) motivate this experiment; they do not establish an improvement for this benchmark.
directions.implementation:
Keep the corrected NextItNet encoder and shared requirements from direction 1. Start with K=64 negatives/positive and calibration t=0.75; consider K=128 only after measuring cost. Extend the family-specific sample_batch negative output to [B,L,K], sampling uniformly from real item IDs while excluding the user's training interactions. Never consult validation targets during training sampling. Compute scores only at pos!=0 and process supervised positions in chunks to avoid a [B,L,K,H] allocation.

For positive logits p:[M] and negative logits n:[M,K], use this stable equivalent of the reference objective:

def gbce_loss(p, n, itemnum, t=0.75):
    import torch.nn.functional as F
    k = n.size(-1)
    alpha = k / max(itemnum - 1, 1)
    beta = 1.0 - t + alpha * t
    return ((beta * F.softplus(-p.float())
             + F.softplus(n.float()).sum(-1)) / (k + 1)).mean()

Derive p and n from model.log2feats(seq) and model.item_emb. Keep inference logits untransformed; the gBCE transformation is a training device. The model class and predictor architecture remain NextItNet. Treat calibration as an adaptation because excluding complete training histories changes the precise sampling distribution assumed by the reference derivation.

directions.description: Use BPR-max with multiple negatives so training emphasizes currently competitive items. Adapt the loss and sampling ideas from [Recurrent Neural Networks with Top-k Gains](https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.03847) and its [official PyTorch implementation](https://github.com/hidasib/GRU4Rec_PyTorch_Official), retaining NextItNet throughout.
directions.implementation:
Keep the shared requirements from direction 1 and the baseline NextItNet architecture. Start with K=32 uniformly sampled negatives per supervised position, excluding training interactions, and regularization coefficient 0.01. Extend sample_batch negatives to [B,L,K] as in direction 2. Compute valid-position positive scores p:[M] and negative scores n:[M,K] through the same encoder and tied embeddings.

def bpr_max_loss(p, n, reg=0.01):
    import torch.nn.functional as F
    p, n = p.float(), n.float()
    log_weights = F.log_softmax(n, dim=-1)
    ranking = -torch.logsumexp(
        log_weights + F.logsigmoid(p[:, None] - n), dim=-1)
    penalty = (log_weights.exp() * n.square()).sum(-1)
    return (ranking + reg * penalty).mean()

Use logsumexp rather than taking a logarithm of an explicitly summed probability. Keep gradients through the softmax negative weights. Start with baseline Adam LR=0.001 and clipping=5.0; evaluate reg=0.1 only as a subsequent isolated change if needed. Score candidates with the single trained NextItNet model; no separate sampler-derived score is added at inference.

directions.description: Add dropout-view contrastive regularization to the same NextItNet network. [DuoRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.05730) and its [author implementation](https://github.com/RuihongQiu/DuoRec/blob/master/recbole/model/sequential_recommender/duorec.py) motivate this training-only adaptation for representation quality.
directions.implementation:
Keep the shared requirements from direction 1. Start with baseline BPR plus 0.05 times contrastive loss, temperature=0.2 and baseline dropout=0.2. Run two stochastic forward passes through the SAME NextItNet instance with shared parameters; do not create a second encoder or checkpoint. Reuse the first pass for recommendation scores. For each nonempty sampled history, extract its final nonpadding feature from both passes:

def last_features(features, seq):
    positions = torch.arange(seq.size(1), device=seq.device).expand_as(seq)
    last = positions.masked_fill(seq.eq(0), -1).amax(1).clamp_min(0)
    return features[torch.arange(seq.size(0), device=seq.device), last]

L2-normalize both feature batches, concatenate into z:[2B,H], and form logits=z@z.T/0.2. Mask self-similarity and train cross-entropy against the matching sequence in the other half. Exclude other rows with identical input histories or identical final training targets from the negative set to reduce false negatives, retaining the designated positive. The auxiliary target is derived solely from the existing training batch. Optimize recommendation and contrastive losses jointly with one optimizer. This is a dropout-view adaptation, not a full DuoRec reproduction. Prediction uses one deterministic eval-mode NextItNet pass and its ordinary candidate dot products; no auxiliary inference branch or predictor architecture change is required.
